briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon, everyone. I will now begin the climate briefing for October 26, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Global Climate Crisis and Call for Urgent Action
sections.content: According to recent major reports, the rate of global warming has nearly doubled since 2010 [179], and extreme weather events are occurring frequently, such as autumn storms hitting Europe and wildfires in the Boundary Waters region nearly tripling in size due to climate change [8, 175]. In particular, in Somalia, El Niño-induced floods, compounded by U.S. military airstrikes, are escalating a humanitarian crisis that threatens civilian safety [194]. Amidst these circumstances, international cooperation dialogues are being held in Korea, China, Japan, and the ASEAN region to find solutions to the climate crisis [3], and the urgency of responding to the climate crisis is being emphasized globally, with Canadian youth, for example, calling for climate action in a landmark trial [178, 180].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Expansion of Domestic Carbon Neutrality Practices and Technological Innovation Efforts
sections.content: Domestically, efforts to practice carbon neutrality in response to the climate crisis are widely expanding. Local-level adaptation efforts are underway, such as the creation of climate change-responsive gardens in Seongdong-gu [5, 15, 16, 17] and the transition to new crop varieties in the Jeju region [1], and citizen-participatory carbon neutrality experience and education programs are being successfully operated by various organizations, including the Ansan Green Environment Center and the Hwaseong Gamtan Expedition [21, 27, 35, 40, 44, 54, 75]. In particular, the South Chungcheong Provincial Council is actively seeking technological solutions, having initiated policy research utilizing Carbon Dioxide Removal (CDR) technologies to achieve the 2045 carbon neutrality goal [22, 23, 24, 34, 36, 37, 46, 49, 63, 64, 72, 77, 82, 85]. Furthermore, expectations for an eco-friendly transition across industries are growing, with the launch of the Carbon Neutrality and Clean Energy Industry Promotion Association and Mokpo Port exploring a transition to a carbon-neutral port [28, 30, 31, 48, 58, 70, 71, 88].

sections.title: 🌱 Tangible Achievements and Expansion Efforts in Renewable Energy Transition
sections.content: This year, the first commemorative ceremony was held after 'Renewable Energy Day' was designated as a legal holiday, reaffirming the importance of the renewable energy transition [94, 128]. Notably, Amorepacific achieved RE100 in five years and received the Presidential Commendation for its contributions to the development of the renewable energy industry [96, 97, 98, 99, 113, 114, 118, 119, 125, 127, 133, 136, 139, 141, 147, 149, 150, 151, 152, 156, 157, 164, 173]. Numerous public institutions and companies, including Korea Western Power, Jeonbuk Development Corporation, NH Nonghyup Bank, and Korea Ocean Business Corporation, also received ministerial commendations for their contributions to renewable energy dissemination and industrial development [92, 95, 100, 102, 104, 105, 106, 110, 112, 115, 120, 123, 124, 129, 131, 134, 138, 142, 143, 144, 145, 154, 159, 160, 162, 165, 166, 167, 168, 172]. Furthermore, the domestic renewable energy ecosystem is expanding through the promotion of large-scale renewable energy projects, such as the joint development of the 435MW 'Incheon Eco Wind Offshore Wind Farm' by Korea South-East Power and EDO Terra One [103, 107, 108, 130, 135, 137, 140, 148, 161, 169, 170, 171].

sections.title: ⚠️ Significant Challenges in Climate Response Funding and Policy
sections.content: Despite efforts to address the climate crisis, significant challenges are emerging in securing funding and setting policy directions. Concerns about fiscal soundness have been raised as half of the 8.5 trillion won climate response fund consists of debt [4], and there have also been observations that job displacement issues could arise during the green transition to carbon neutrality [73]. During the 2026 parliamentary audit, alongside controversies over the effectiveness of renewable energy safety inspections due to delays in power grid construction [117], concerns were raised that a significant downward adjustment of the Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) could collapse the renewable energy industry ecosystem, including solar power [132]. Furthermore, social discussions on the direction of energy policy are active, with arguments emerging that nuclear power should be prioritized over renewable energy when pursuing coal phase-out policies [146]. Internationally, Alaska's senatorial candidates have largely avoided mentioning climate change [176], and candidates in the U.S. midterm elections have adopted a strategy of speaking quietly about climate change [192], indicating anticipated difficulties in securing political will.

briefing.closing: Today's briefing highlighted the severity of the climate crisis, various response efforts both domestically and internationally, and the challenges that need to be addressed. Our collective attention and action are vital for a sustainable future. This concludes today's climate briefing.
